items.title: Branford Marsalis — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: When I was on alto, I was listening to Wayne.

ctx.x: you start to, cause you know it’s incumbent on you to do your research, to do your historical research, to figure out how the music got to this level. So when you went back, who were the people, who were the folks that you started, like you said…. Well, Johnny Hodges, but who were you listening to to develop that sound?

When I was on alto, I was listening to Wayne. And when I switched to tenor I started listening to Bird. Genius. But I often, I mean the horn is kind of a medium to me. It’s not the thing, the ideas are the thing. And those ideas are interchangeable regardless of the instrument. So when I’m listening to those guys, I’m trying to capture their sound. And I’m really paying attention to how they react to the rhythm section and I’m trying to learn the rhythm, because each guy has a unique way of playing, employing,…
What did you think about Ornette on tenor?
